html:
The laws made by Solon when he was chief magistrate of Athens in 594 BCE, at a time when the city was close to civil war between rich and poor.

Many poor farmers had fallen into debt, and some had been enslaved or sold abroad. Solon:

  • cancelled debts secured on land and people, a measure called the "shaking off of burdens"
  • banned enslaving Athenians for debt and bought back some who had been sold
  • divided citizens into four classes by the size of their harvests, and opened offices to wealth instead of birth alone
  • let every citizen appeal to a court of the people
  • repealed Draco's laws except those on homicide

He then left Athens for ten years so he would not be pressed to change them. His poems defending the reforms survive in part. He pleased neither side fully, and within decades Pisistratus seized power. Still, Solon's laws laid the ground for the democracy of Cleisthenes and for Athenian democracy.
sum: The laws made by Solon when he was chief magistrate of Athens in 594 BCE, at a time when the city was close to civil war between rich and poor.
